newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pennzoil sees output hike in Venezuela's B2X68/79.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil sees output hike in Venezuela's B2X68/79.

text.p: U.S. oil company Pennzoil expects to produce at least 110 million barrels over 20 years under its newly acquired contract to operate the B2X.68/79 oilfield in western Venezuela, a company official said Tuesday.
Carl Evans, Pennzoil's Latin America chief, said he hoped production would reach 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) in seven years from 2,500 bpd currently.
Pennzoil won the 20-year operator's contract with a bid of $46 million in a round that has attracted companies from all corners of the world.
Evans said he planned to spend more than $100 million in capital expenditure in the next few years, and this figure would rise if more reserves were found.
"Venezuela is the Saudi Arabia of Latin America. The opportunities that I can see for this type of activity are unique to Venezuela," Evans said.
Pennzoil has a 60 percent stake in a consortium which includes Saudi Arabia's Nimir Petroleum with 20 percent and Venezuela's Ehcopek and Cartera de Inversiones with 10 percent each.
The B2X68/79 field brings Pennzoil's contracts in Venezuela to two, with its East Falcon contract awarded in 1993. Falcon was still in development and producing just 1,000 bpd, Evans said.
